**Analyzing Go command glob**

I’m exploring the command glob for Go files, like `**/*.go`, and how shell globstar matches various internal functions. It seems the function parser needs to count declarations and references for specific internal names. Maybe I can automate this using Perl to extract declarations and count occurrences throughout the repository. I'm thinking of distinguishing method names and excluding tests, while also considering a regex to capture receiver methods. I want to focus on gathering and processing this data efficiently!

args.command: shopt -s globstar; perl -0777 -e 'my (%decl,%c); for my $f (glob("internal/**/*.go")){open my $h,"<",$f or next; local $/; my $s=<$h>; while($s =~ /^func\s+(?:\([^\n]*?\)\s+)?([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(/mg){$decl{$1}{$f}=1} } for my $f (glob("**/*.go")){open my $h,"<",$f or next; local $/; my $s=<$h>; while($s =~ /\b([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*\(/g){$c{$1}++} } for my $n (sort {$c{$b}<=>$c{$a}} keys %decl){my $d=scalar keys %{$decl{$n}}; my $v=($c{$n}//0)-$d; print "$v $n ($d decls) ",join(",",keys %{$decl{$n}}),"\n" if $v > 5}'
